Node child of node-gyp/python making outbound to GitHub dead-drop or anomalous web service during install AIexfil Medium
Catches the Miasma exfiltration step: after the binding.gyp command-expansion fires, the spawned node.exe (running index.js) beacons cloud credentials and CI tokens out to attacker-controlled GitHub repositories or webhook services. Pivots on the rare combination of node.exe with a node-gyp/python ancestor making outbound TCP to api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, or first-seen external hosts. Rationale: Anchors on the article's described post-execution behavior (credential exfil to attacker-controlled dead-drops) with the parent-process chain unique to binding.gyp abuse. Corroborating sources (Endor Labs, Morphisec, OX Security) confirm Miasma exfils to GitHub dead-drop repos and uses Workers/webhook bouncers; this detection requires both the gyp ancestry AND the suspicious destination to fire, keeping FPs manageable while catching the campaign-specific exfil shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/malicious-payload-in-ai-sdk-ollama-npm-package • https://www.morphisec.com/blog/its-in-your-ai-assistant-now-shai-hulud-wave-3-and-the-miasma-worm-targeting-npm/ • https://www.ox.security/blog/600000-monthly-downloads-affected-miasma-supply-chain-attack-is-back-on-npm/
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1552.001 T1041
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm packages whose postinstall hook fetches assets from raw.githubusercontent.com (e.g. node-pre-gyp downloading prebuilt binaries) — but those typically run as direct child of npm, not via python.exe (gyp) chain
  • node-gyp packages that pull source tarballs from GitHub during configure step (rare; node-pre-gyp uses HTTP downloader)
  • CI runners that genuinely push to api.github.com via node-based GitHub API client called from a build hook
  • Cloudflare Workers used by an org's internal build accelerator service
Suppression filter
| where not (ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-pre-gyp","prebuild-install") and DstHostname has "objects.githubusercontent.com")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the spawning binding.gyp content and the node process's full argv; identify which npm package owns the source path. Check whether the GitHub destination repo is org-controlled (legitimate) or an externally owned account (likely dead-drop). Step 2 — Contain: kill the node.exe PID, isolate the device, and immediately rotate every credential reachable from the host — focus first on the developer's GitHub PAT (worm publishes via it), npm publish token, AWS keys in ~/.aws/credentials, .npmrc auth, kubeconfig, Vault tokens, GCP/Azure CLI cache. Step 3 — Hunt: query GitHub audit log for new repository creations under the developer's user account in the last 24h (Miasma creates ephemeral dead-drop repos); search ImNetworkSession for any other node.exe egress to the same destination from CI runners in the last 7 days; check npm registry for unauthorized package publications under the dev's maintainer accounts.
let gyp_node_children = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "node.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","cmd.exe","sh","bash")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gyp.py","binding.gyp","node-gyp")
        or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project ProcSpawnTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessId, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com",".workers.dev","webhook.site","ngrok.io","hooks.slack.com","discord.com/api/webhooks","transfer.sh","file.io","0x0.st")
   or RemoteIPType == "Public"
| join kind=inner gyp_node_children on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ProcessId
| where Timestamp between (ProcSpawnTime .. ProcSpawnTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, GypParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine1
| order by Timestamp desc
let gyp_node_children = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]node(\.exe)?$"
    | where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)[\\/](python3?|cmd|sh|bash)(\.exe)?$"
    | where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("gyp.py","binding.gyp","node-gyp")
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project ProcSpawnTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ParentProcessCommandLine;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstHostname has_any ("api.github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com",".workers.dev","webhook.site","ngrok.io","hooks.slack.com","discord.com","transfer.sh","file.io","0x0.st")
| join kind=inner gyp_node_children on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (ProcSpawnTime .. ProcSpawnTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes, ParentProcessCommandLine
source:(windows.sysmon OR crowdstrike) @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) (@DestinationHostname:(*api.github.com* OR *raw.githubusercontent.com* OR *.workers.dev OR *webhook.site* OR *ngrok.io* OR *hooks.slack.com* OR *discord.com* OR *transfer.sh* OR *file.io* OR *0x0.st*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i ParentBaseFileName=/^(python3?|cmd|sh|bash)\.exe$/i ParentCommandLine=/(gyp\.py|binding\.gyp|node-gyp)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(api\.github\.com|raw\.githubusercontent\.com|objects\.githubusercontent\.com|\.workers\.dev$|webhook\.site|ngrok\.io|hooks\.slack\.com|discord\.com|transfer\.sh|file\.io|0x0\.st)/i}, field=aid, include=[DomainName, ContextImageFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, CommandLine, ParentCommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="node.exe" AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","cmd.exe","sh","bash") AND (Processes.parent_process="*gyp*" OR Processes.parent_process="*binding.gyp*" OR Processes.parent_process="*node-gyp*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_id Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process Processes._time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename _time as proc_time process_id as suspect_pid | join type=inner dest suspect_pid [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="api.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="raw.githubusercontent.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.workers.dev" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.webhook.site" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.ngrok.io" OR All_Traffic.dest="hooks.slack.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="discord.com") AND All_Traffic.app="node.exe" by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | rename src as dest dest as net_dest app as suspect_pid]
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry

status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:

date: 2026/05/02

            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

SecurityEvent

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or SHA1 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or MD5 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or SHA1 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108") or MD5 in~ ("ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] MFA approval within minutes of inbound external Microsoft Teams chat · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)

External MS Teams chat invite from IT-impersonating unmanaged or federated tenant AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for inbound Microsoft Teams chat invitations from external/guest users whose display name or sender domain impersonates internal IT/helpdesk/MSP functions — the exact technique Cloaked Ursa and UNC6692 used to initiate the social-engineering conversation before requesting MFA approval. Rationale: Maps to the article's central narrative — external Teams chat from an unmanaged/federated tenant whose sender display name impersonates IT/helpdesk/MSP. Combines the external-user predicate (#EXT#/onmicrosoft.com/UserType=Guest) with the IT-impersonation lexicon Unit 42 calls out as the lowered-suspicion lure.
ATT&CKT1566.003 T1656
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate inbound chat from a contracted MSP whose display name genuinely includes 'IT Support'
  • Vendor partners pinged via cross-tenant federation for break/fix conversations
  • Internal IT delegate accounts that are mailbox-shared with external collaborators
  • Sales reps from security/IT vendors initiating prospecting chats
  • Conference / training organizers whose tenant names contain 'IT'
Suppression filter
| where UserId !endswith "@your-trusted-msp.com" and UserId !endswith "@your-contracted-vendor.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on UserId (sender), ClientIP, and UserAgent — check whether the sender tenant is on your federation Allow list and whether the sender domain typosquats your IT/MSP brand. Look up the recipient's recent chat/MFA history. 2) Contain: if confirmed external impersonation, remove the recipient's MFA-pending session, force token revocation (`Revoke-MgUserSignInSession`), and add the sender tenant or domain to the Teams external-domain Block list; if widespread, restrict Teams federation to allow-list mode (Figure 3 of the article). 3) Hunt: pivot on sender IP to find other recipients hit by the same external tenant; check SigninLogs for MFA prompts to those recipients in the 30 min window after each chat; check CloudAppEvents for any file/URL shared in the chat body.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded","ChatRetrieved","MeetingDetailMessaged")
| extend RawStr = tostring(RawEventData), ActObjStr = tostring(ActivityObjects)
| where AccountType in~ ("Guest","External") or RawStr has_any ("#EXT#","onmicrosoft.com")
| where ActObjStr has_any ("IT Support","IT Department","Help Desk","Helpdesk","Service Desk","IT Admin","Security Team","SOC Team","Managed Service","MSP")
| project Timestamp, ActionType, AccountDisplayName, AccountId, AccountType, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent, ObjectName, ActivityObjects, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded","MemberRoleChanged")
| extend ParamsStr = tostring(Parameters)
| where UserType in ("Guest","External") or UserId has_any ("#EXT#","#ext#","onmicrosoft.com")
| where ParamsStr has_any ("IT Support","IT Department","Help Desk","Helpdesk","Service Desk","IT Admin","Security Team","SOC Team","Managed Service","MSP")
| project TimeGenerated, Operation, UserId, UserType, ClientIP, UserAgent, OfficeObjectId, ParamsStr
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(office365 OR azure.activeDirectory) (@Workload:MicrosoftTeams OR @evt.name:("ChatCreated" OR "MessageSent" OR "MemberAdded")) (@UserType:(Guest OR External) OR @UserId:(*#EXT#* OR *onmicrosoft.com*)) ("IT Support" OR "IT Department" OR "Help Desk" OR Helpdesk OR "Service Desk" OR "Security Team" OR "Managed Service" OR MSP)
APPLICATION
`cim_Authentication_indexes` sourcetype IN ("o365:management:activity","ms:o365:management") Workload="MicrosoftTeams" Operation IN ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded","MemberRoleChanged") 
| spath input=Parameters 
| eval is_external=if(match(UserId,"(?i)#EXT#|onmicrosoft\.com") OR UserType IN ("Guest","External"),1,0) 
| where is_external=1 
| eval impersonation=if(match(_raw,"(?i)(IT\s?Support|Help\s?Desk|Helpdesk|Service\s?Desk|IT\s?Department|IT\s?Admin|MSP|Managed\s?Service|Security\s?Team|SOC\s?Team)"),1,0) 
| where impersonation=1 
| table _time UserId UserType ClientIP UserAgent Operation OfficeWorkload Parameters 
| sort - _time
MFA approval within minutes of inbound external Microsoft Teams chat AIExploitation High
Correlates an inbound external Teams chat to a user with a successful MFA-satisfied sign-in by that same user inside a 30-minute window. Surfaces the Cloaked Ursa / UNC6692 pattern where the 'IT technician' chat is immediately followed by a victim-approved MFA push. Rationale: 30-minute window pairing an inbound external Teams chat with an MFA-satisfied sign-in by the same recipient maps directly to the article's narrative — 'IT technician' chat → 'approve this MFA' → compromise. Time-window correlation is the noise-killer the BluRaven kb prescribes for this scenario.
ATT&CKT1621 T1566.003
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MSP help desk genuinely fixing a sign-in issue with a real user
  • Internal IT walking a user through SSO enrollment via a federated tenant
  • Vendor support chats where a user simultaneously re-authenticates to the same vendor portal
  • Conference Wi-Fi MFA prompt happening to fire during an unrelated external chat
  • Newly-onboarded user receiving both a welcome chat from an external HR consultant AND completing initial MFA setup
Suppression filter
| where SenderUpn !endswith "@your-trusted-msp.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the chat sender's UserId — verify whether the sender tenant is on the Teams federation Allow list. Pull the SigninLogs MFA detail (was it push, SMS, OAuth code, FIDO2?) and the destination IP / country. 2) Contain: if the IP geo, ASN, or device fingerprint of the MFA-approved sign-in doesn't match the victim's baseline, revoke sessions immediately (`Revoke-MgUserSignInSession`), force credential reset, and block the sender tenant in Teams external-access settings. 3) Hunt: pivot on the MFA-success IP for the next 24 hours across SigninLogs — likely the same IP is harvesting other accounts the attacker chatted; also check OfficeActivity MailItemsAccessed, InboxRuleCreated, and CloudAppEvents OAuth grants under the compromised UPN.
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let ExternalChats = CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
    | where ActionType in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded")
    | extend RawStr = tostring(RawEventData)
    | where AccountType in~ ("Guest","External") or RawStr has_any ("#EXT#","onmicrosoft.com")
    | extend Recipient = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ActivityObjects))[0].Name)
    | project ChatTime = Timestamp, SenderUpn = AccountDisplayName, SenderIP = IPAddress, Recipient, ActionType;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where AuthenticationRequirement =~ "multiFactorAuthentication"
| extend AuthDetailStr = tostring(AuthenticationDetails)
| where AuthDetailStr has_any ("Mobile app notification","PhoneAppNotification","OAuth Verify","Authenticator App")
| join kind=inner ExternalChats on $left.AccountUpn == $right.Recipient
| where Timestamp between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, ChatTime)
| project ChatTime, MfaApprovalTime = Timestamp, DelayMinutes, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, Application, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, SenderUpn, SenderIP
| order by MfaApprovalTime desc
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let ExternalChats = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where OfficeWorkload =~ "MicrosoftTeams"
    | where Operation in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded")
    | where UserType in ("Guest","External") or UserId has_any ("#EXT#","#ext#","onmicrosoft.com")
    | extend ParamsStr = tostring(Parameters)
    | extend Recipient = extract(@"(?i)([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})", 1, ParamsStr)
    | project ChatTime = TimeGenerated, SenderUpn = UserId, SenderIP = ClientIP, Recipient;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where AuthenticationRequirement =~ "multiFactorAuthentication"
| extend AuthMethods = tostring(AuthenticationMethodsUsed)
| where AuthMethods has_any ("Mobile app notification","PhoneAppNotification","Microsoft Authenticator")
| join kind=inner ExternalChats on $left.UserPrincipalName == $right.Recipient
| where TimeGenerated between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, ChatTime)
| project ChatTime, MfaApprovalTime = TimeGenerated, DelayMinutes, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, AppDisplayName, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, SenderUpn, SenderIP
| order by MfaApprovalTime desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:0 @properties.authenticationRequirement:multiFactorAuthentication (@properties.authenticationMethodsUsed:("Mobile app notification" OR "PhoneAppNotification" OR "Microsoft Authenticator"))

| AuthenticationMethod=/(Mobile app notification|PhoneAppNotification|Microsoft Authenticator)/i
| groupBy([UserPrincipalName, IPAddress], function=count())

Activity involving ommicrosoft.com Cloaked-Ursa Teams typosquat AIDelivery High
Direct IOC hunt for the ommicrosoft.com typosquat domain referenced by Unit 42 in connection with Cloaked Ursa / Midnight Blizzard Teams credential-harvesting infrastructure. Sweeps Teams/Office activity, AAD sign-ins, DNS resolutions, and proxy traffic for any reference to the domain. Rationale: ommicrosoft.com is the only hard IOC in the article — a single-character typosquat of microsoft.com that Unit 42 ties to Cloaked Ursa Teams credential-harvesting. Any resolution, web request, sign-in reference, or Teams artifact mentioning this string is high-fidelity. Union covers chat, sign-in, DNS, and proxy surfaces because the same domain may surface across all four during the kill chain.
ATT&CKT1583.001 T1566.003 T1656
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution Web Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform / TIP fetching the IOC for analysis
  • Security researcher manually pivoting on the domain
  • Sandbox detonation submitting URL for analysis
  • Phishing-simulation vendor staging a lookalike for an awareness exercise
  • Mail security gateway sandbox following the link from a quarantined message
Suppression filter
| where SrcIP !in ("<SOC sandbox IP>","<TIP enrichment IP>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source — internal SOC tooling vs end-user host. If a Teams sender UPN or sign-in UPN contains the domain, treat as confirmed Cloaked Ursa attempted contact. 2) Contain: sinkhole / block ommicrosoft.com at the proxy and resolver tier, block the sender tenant in Teams external access, and (for any user with a sign-in attempt or click) revoke sessions and force credential rotation. Push an Entra ID Conditional Access policy blocking sign-ins where Resource or App matches the IOC. 3) Hunt: pivot on the resolved IP(s) over the last 90 days in DnsEvents / DeviceNetworkEvents and proxy logs; check UrlClickEvents for any click-through; review OfficeActivity for chat history from the sender tenant to enumerate additional victims.
let IOC = dynamic(["ommicrosoft.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceNetworkEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC) or AdditionalFields has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="NetworkEvents", DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
    (UrlClickEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where Url has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="UrlClickEvents", DeviceName="", AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName="", RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP=tostring(IPAddress)),
    (CloudAppEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
        | extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData), Acts = tostring(ActivityObjects)
        | where Raw has_any (IOC) or Acts has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="Teams", DeviceName="", AccountUpn=AccountDisplayName, InitiatingProcessFileName=ActionType, RemoteUrl=ObjectName, RemoteIP=IPAddress),
    (AADSignInEventsBeta
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where AccountUpn has_any (IOC) or AlternateSignInName has_any (IOC) or ResourceDisplayName has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="AADSignIn", DeviceName=DeviceName, AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName=Application, RemoteUrl=ResourceDisplayName, RemoteIP=IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["ommicrosoft.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (OfficeActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where UserId has_any (IOC) or tostring(Parameters) has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="OfficeActivity", Operation, User=UserId, SrcIP=ClientIP, Detail=tostring(Parameters)),
    (SigninLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where UserPrincipalName has_any (IOC) or AppDisplayName has_any (IOC) or ResourceDisplayName has_any (IOC) or AlternateSignInName has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="SigninLogs", Operation=OperationName, User=UserPrincipalName, SrcIP=IPAddress, Detail=strcat(AppDisplayName," | ",ResultDescription)),
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Name has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Operation=QueryTypeName, User="", SrcIP=ClientIP, Detail=Name),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationHostName has_any (IOC) or RequestURL has_any (IOC) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="Proxy/CSL", Operation=DeviceAction, User=SourceUserName, SrcIP=SourceIP, Detail=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

SecurityEvent

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

status: experimental

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1204.002

    category: process_creation

            - '\pwsh.exe'

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Talos weekly prevalent malware SHA256 IOC sweep (Coinminer / Procpatcher / KMS activator) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts process executions and file writes matching the five SHA256 hashes Talos called out as the week's most prevalent malware in their 2026-06-04 newsletter telemetry roundup. Covers Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (sample.exe), W32.C0AD494457-95 (f_000b97.html), and PUA.Win.Tool.Kmsactivator (AutoPico.exe). Rationale: Detection is grounded on the five SHA256 hashes Talos explicitly named in the 'Most prevalent malware files' block (VID001.exe Coinminer, sample.exe Procpatcher, f_000b97.html W32.C0AD494457-95, AutoPico.exe Kmsactivator, plus the fifth truncated entry). These are confirmed-bad per Talos detection names — file-reputation match is the highest-fidelity signal possible from this article. No external sources cross-checked: the IOC list is a weekly Talos telemetry snapshot from today's date with no second source yet published.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1496 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security analysts intentionally detonating samples in a sandbox / malware-analysis VM (especially analysts retrieving Talos-flagged hashes for testing)
  • AutoPico.exe / KMS activator hash firing on unlicensed Windows installs (common in test/lab environments and unmanaged dev boxes)
  • f_000b97.html cached in browser cache directories from a benign visit — file write triggers without execution (review FolderPath for browser cache paths before escalating)
  • EDR vendor sample-collection / threat intel platforms (CrowdStrike, MDE attack surface reduction telemetry) pulling sample copies for analysis
  • Legitimate AV scanners writing the sample to quarantine — initiating process being the AV engine itself
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !contains "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !contains "\\Sandbox\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","CSFalconService.exe","SenseIR.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the matching event's FolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, and AccountName. If folder is a known sandbox/quarantine path (e.g. C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine, sandbox VM paths) or parent is an AV engine, downgrade. Confirm the Talos detection name from the case statement against the article's labelling. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR network containment. Kill the live process tree; quarantine the file. For Coinminer (VID001.exe) check for persistence via Run keys and scheduled tasks; for Procpatcher review which process was patched (often AV/EDR tampering). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessParentFileName to find the delivery vector (browser download? email attachment? USB?). Sweep the rest of the fleet for the same SHA256 over 30 days and for the parent's hash. If KMS activator triggered, audit the host for other PUA / cracked software via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory.

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

let BadDomains = dynamic(["kongtuke.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe", "afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638", "a31f222fc283227f5e7988d1ad9c0aecd66d58bb7b4d8518ae23e110308dbf91", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "bf9672ec85283fdf002d83662f0b08b7", "cc4d231df34e57f59eb970353c7d9de2", "7bdbd180c081fa63ca94f9c22c457376"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Critical

Miasma npm Supply Chain Attack: Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp

StepSecurity
2026-06-04 5 use cases 3 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

self-replicating worm is spreading across the npm registry using binding.gyp, a file that triggers code execution during npm install without touching package.json scripts. The attack bypasses conventional security tools and has already compromised dozens of packages across multiple maintainer accounts.

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Miasma npm Supply Chain Attack: Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path · [LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path AICommand & Control High
Hunts the specific KongTuke (TAG-124 / 404 TDS) command-and-control infrastructure named in the Talos case study: outbound HTTP to 144.31.221.82 on TCP/6060 with a URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint. Single-IOC alerting because all three values are article-named. Rationale: Single high-confidence IOC bundle straight from the Talos case-study paragraph: IP 144.31.221.82, TCP/6060, URL path /capcha9856. The /capcha* fingerprint is corroborated by Recorded Future (TAG-124), Red Canary KongTuke profile, and malware-traffic-analysis.net Jan 2026 KongTuke ClickFix capture. Cross-checked via WebSearch — KongTuke is a real, active TDS. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base • https://www.malware-traffic-analysis.net/2026/01/08/index.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal pentest or red-team rehearsal targeting the same IOC after reading the Talos blog
  • Threat-intel platform or DFIR sandbox automatically dialling out to known-bad C2 for verification (e.g. JoeSandbox, ANY.RUN agent on a corp jump host)
  • Threat-hunt tooling that replays packet captures with the destination IP rewritten for test purposes
  • Security awareness training simulator using captured KongTuke traffic
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("smss.exe","wininit.exe") and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","sbox","detonation","malsandbox"))
Response runbook
Triage: Confirm the source host is a real production endpoint, then pull DeviceProcessEvents on it for ±30 min around the connection. Look for cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → curl.exe chain that Talos documented. Check Defender/AMP for any blocked-detection signatures on the same host. Contain: Isolate the host via Defender for Endpoint / Falcon Network Containment. Block 144.31.221.82 + the /capcha URL pattern at the firewall and proxy. Force-reset the logged-in user's credentials. Hunt: Sweep the entire estate for any other endpoint connecting to 144.31.221.82, port 6060, or any URL containing /capcha. Check WordPress/CMS site referrer logs for which compromised site redirected the user (TDS chains). Submit the IP to TI vendors and enrol the URL-path pattern into the proxy as a hunt rule.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82"
   or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
   or RemoteUrl has "/capcha9856"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Cisco" or DeviceProduct has "Firepower" or DeviceProduct has "Secure Firewall" or isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82"
   or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
   or RequestURL has "/capcha9856"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort,
          RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: KongTuke TDS C2 to 144.31.221.82 / capcha URL Path
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a01
description: Detects outbound network traffic to KongTuke TDS C2 infrastructure (144.31.221.82:6060) or any URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint reported by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
  - https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '144.31.221.82'
  selection_port_path:
    DestinationPort: 6060
    DestinationHostname|contains: '/capcha'
  selection_path:
    Url|contains: '/capcha9856'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_port_path or selection_path
falsepositives:

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:cisco-firepower OR source:cisco_secure_firewall) AND (@DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 OR (@DestinationPort:6060 AND @DestinationHostname:*\/capcha*) OR @network.destination.ip:144.31.221.82 OR @url:*\/capcha9856*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82" OR RemotePort=6060)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/capcha/i}, field=aid, include=[DomainName], mode=left)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
